'''''Lathyrus sylvestris''''', the '''flat pea''' or '''narrow-leaved everlasting-pea''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the pea and bean family [[Fabaceae]]. It is native to parts of Africa, Europe, and Asia.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 14 January 2018}}</ref>

The narrow-leaved everlasting-pea forms a mat of herbage. The stems are winged. Each leaf is made up of two elongated leaflets. The flowers are pink. The fruit is a [[legume]] pod about {{convert|2|in|cm|0}} long.<ref name=usda>[https://plants.usda.gov/factsheet/pdf/fs_lasy.pdf ''Lathyrus sylvestris''.] USDA NRCS Plant Fact Sheet.</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Eucera longicornis - Lathyrus sylvestris - Keila.jpg|thumb|right|Pollination by long-horned bee]]
The narrow-leaved everlasting-pea is a perennial plant which can grow {{convert|200|cm|0|abbr=on}} by climbing with its [[tendril]]s. Without any support it can reach about {{convert|75|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall. The stem is floppy and flat with wide wings. The leaves are alternate with short winged stalks and stipules. The leaf blades are pinnate with a single pair of narrow lanceolate leaflets with entire margins and three tendrils. The [[inflorescence]] has a long stem and three to ten pinkish-red flowers. These have five sepals and five petals and are irregular. The uppermost petal is known as the "standard", the lateral two as the "wings" and the lowest two are joined to form the "keel". There are ten stamens and a single carpel. The fruit is a long pod containing five to fifteen seeds.<ref name=NatureGate>{{cite web |url=http://www.luontoportti.com/suomi/en/kukkakasvit/narrow-leaved-everlasting-pea |title=Narrow-leaved Everlasting Pea: ''Lathyrus sylvestris''|publisher=NatureGate |access-date=2013-12-30}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
The narrow-leaved everlasting-pea is native to parts of Africa, Europe and Asia.<ref name=grin/> Its natural habitat is forest edges, sparse broad-leaved hillside forests, dry hillside meadows, hedgerows, embankments and waste ground. It uses its tendrils to scramble over plants, shrubs and the lower branches of trees.<ref name=NatureGate/>

==Uses==
This plant is sometimes used to control [[erosion]] and for this purpose it is generally planted along with a grass species. It can do well in highly disturbed habitat. There is a [[cultivar]] called 'Lathco'.<ref name=usda/>
